programme.title: Agency Transfer Research Programme
programme.subtitle: Frontier AI, harmful manipulation, and democratic power
programme.lead: The next Cambridge Analytica will be a system.
programme.scope_statement: Manipulation at scale facilitated by frontier AI: what is happening, what may be coming, and how democracies can mitigate the danger.
programme.secondary_lens: Manipulation as a mechanism for the extreme concentration of political and epistemic power.
programme.thesis: Frontier AI can make influence more scalable, adaptive, persistent, and infrastructural. The democratic risk lies not only in false content, but in concentrated control over the systems that shape attention, trust, choice, dependency, and the evidence needed to contest them.
programme.author: Miguel Guerrero
programme.claim_boundary: The programme does not establish a closed adaptive influence loop, authentic audience exposure, durable agency erosion, a prevalence estimate, or an AI-attributable electoral effect.

evidence_grades.label: Established evidence
evidence_grades.definition: Directly observed or source-verified within the stated system, protocol, and endpoint.

evidence_grades.label: Strong inference
evidence_grades.definition: A conclusion well supported by established observations but not directly measured at the claimed layer.

evidence_grades.label: Plausible hypothesis
evidence_grades.definition: A mechanism consistent with available evidence that still requires direct testing.

evidence_grades.label: Speculative scenario
evidence_grades.definition: A conditional pathway whose conjunction, probability, or threshold is not established.

evidence_grades.label: Open question
evidence_grades.definition: A material uncertainty for which the programme does not yet have sufficient evidence.

research_parts.title: From output to operationalisation
research_parts.question: When does model or served-system capability become an operational influence system?
research_parts.observed_unit: Paired red-team objectives, exploratory probes, forensic trace bundles, and access-to-control methods runs.
research_parts.strongest_supported_claim: Recorded served routes produced recognisable campaign-planning elements under bounded conditions, while the conversion from model access to a reproducible intervention remained technically fragile.
research_parts.claim_ceiling: No successful intervention, autonomous execution, authentic audience contact, persuasion, manipulation of a real person, or electoral effect.
research_parts.counting_note: These are different evidence units, may partially overlap, and must not be summed.

research_parts.title: Capability and measurement
research_parts.question: What can current instruments say about manipulation-relevant frontier-model behaviour, and where does the measurement system fail?
research_parts.observed_unit: A six-instrument Evaluation Registry and a recovered APE-120 audit across served model conditions.
research_parts.strongest_supported_claim: Persuasion attempts were common among valid APE-120 observations, but route instability, missingness, evaluator validity, and coverage prevented every prespecified confirmatory model estimate and any defensible pooled longitudinal index.
research_parts.claim_ceiling: No pooled manipulation score, no human persuasion estimate, no model safety ranking, and no defensible longitudinal frontier trend.

research_parts.title: Election evidence and the effect gap
research_parts.question: What do public election records establish about AI-mediated influence operations, exposure, and downstream effects?
research_parts.observed_unit: A purposive claim-level evidence index of incidents, mechanisms, distribution evidence, attribution, and institutional response.
research_parts.strongest_supported_claim: Public records establish selected operations, mechanisms, attribution evidence, distribution proxies, and institutional responses more often than authentic exposure, durable human effects, or electoral consequences.
research_parts.claim_ceiling: No prevalence estimate and no validated national electoral effect attributable to AI-mediated manipulation.
research_parts.counting_note: Relational rows and catalogue entries are not incident counts. The public release contains six documented-manipulation records.

research_parts.title: Policy evidence and intervention
research_parts.question: Where can democracies interrupt the causal chain, under whose authority, and with what evidence and rights burden?
research_parts.observed_unit: A causal policy atlas of control families, implementations, claims, sources, mechanisms, decision gates, and research gaps.
research_parts.strongest_supported_claim: The intervention portfolio is broad, but checked and bounded evidence of effectiveness remains sparse; the current atlas supports causal mapping and research triage, not a numeric policy ranking.
research_parts.claim_ceiling: No globally representative policy-effect estimate and no composite 'best policy' score.

artifacts.title: Harmful Manipulation and Election Security: The Capability–Deployment–Effect Gap
artifacts.role: Programme-level flagship synthesis and primary editorial spine.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Programme synthesis, not a single-estimand study; no closed adaptive loop, authentic exposure, durable agency erosion, prevalence estimate, or AI-attributable electoral effect.
artifacts.publication_note: Canonical source file selected; stable web/PDF publication URL still required.

artifacts.title: Client-observed served-system evidence bundles
artifacts.role: Deep forensic subset of the broader Part I exploratory programme.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Output-level planning evidence from an unidentified served route; no checkpoint identity, autonomous execution, exposure, persuasion, or electoral effect.
artifacts.responsible_release_note: Raw harmful prompts, campaign-ready outputs, credentials, and operational traces remain withheld.

artifacts.title: Agency Transfer Lab
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Validates deterministic harness behaviour, replay, persistence, migration, and integrity; it does not measure frontier capability, persuasion, behaviour change, agency transfer, actor uplift, or electoral impact.
artifacts.publication_note: Public deployment may be linked. Private source repository must not be linked.

artifacts.title: From open weights to reproducible intervention
artifacts.role: Access-to-control methods study and public fail-closed contracts.
artifacts.source_version: v1.1 methods note and public contract series
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Documents technical process and failed or incomplete conversion attempts; no saved behavioural intervention or successful model modification is established.

artifacts.title: Controlled evaluation evidence
artifacts.role: Private logs, outputs, grader traces, reviewer mappings, validation material, and encrypted archives.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Supports controlled validation and audit only; it is not a public artifact.
artifacts.responsible_release_note: Do not publish or link the private control plane.

artifacts.title: Frontier Evaluation Registry
artifacts.role: Source-linked release map retaining benchmark-native outcomes and comparability limits.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: No cross-instrument scalar, ranking, latent capability estimate, or causal time trend.
artifacts.publication_note: Currently occupies the programme root and will be preserved under Part II with redirects.

artifacts.title: APE-120 recovered audit
artifacts.role: Direct primary-research audit of instructed persuasion attempts across served conditions.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Descriptive attempt evidence only; no condition passed the confirmatory gate and no model-level efficacy or safety claim is licensed.

artifacts.title: Agency Transfer Benchmark dataset
artifacts.role: Aggregate-and-provenance-only public mirror for Part II.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Aggregate and provenance data only; raw harmful generations are excluded.

artifacts.title: AI, Elections and Agency Transfer Evidence Index
artifacts.role: Claim-level evidence index and public election-case dataset.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Purposive evidence corpus, not a prevalence sample; public records do not validate national vote effects attributable to AI-mediated manipulation.
artifacts.publication_note: The site must display source version, public release version, research cutoff, and site snapshot separately.

artifacts.title: Agency Transfer Policy Atlas
artifacts.role: Causal evidence map of interventions against AI-mediated manipulation.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Beta causal map and research-triage artifact; no numeric policy ranking or globally representative effect estimate.
artifacts.publication_note: The site must distinguish policy adoption, mechanism evidence, effect evidence, operational maturity, and source-verification depth.

artifacts.title: The Persuasion Machines: Frontier AI, Persuasion, and the Risk of Harmful Manipulation
artifacts.role: Accessible adjacent synthesis for policy and general audiences.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Adjacent synthesis; not a substitute for the flagship paper or its source-specific claim ceilings.
artifacts.publication_note: Standalone canonical file and durable public URL still require selection.

artifacts.title: The next Cambridge Analytica will be a system
artifacts.role: One-page explanation of the CDE Gap and the four research parts.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Editorial summary only; figures must remain bound to the denominators and caveats in the flagship paper.
artifacts.publication_note: Canonical file selected provisionally; durable public URL still required.

artifacts.title: Harmful Manipulation and Election Security
artifacts.role: Visual overview of the evidence rift, the four research parts, and the security response.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Visual synthesis; numbers are evidence observed at different layers and are not a single funnel or additive score.
artifacts.publication_note: One poster must be designated canonical; older visual variants should be archived.

artifacts.title: Brazil 2026 harmful-manipulation explainer
artifacts.role: Synthetic scenario explainer illustrating how capability, targeting, distribution, and feedback could be joined.
artifacts.claim_ceiling: Illustrative synthetic scenario; not evidence of a real operation, authentic exposure, behaviour change, or electoral effect.
artifacts.responsible_release_note: Do not publish temporary-host URLs. Review the final cut for operational detail before durable release.

known_blockers: Publish the flagship paper at a stable web and PDF URL.
Select and publish the standalone canonical white paper.
Select one canonical poster and archive variants.
Publish the one-page brief at a durable URL.
Move explainer-video masters from temporary hosting to a durable host, then add poster frames, captions, and transcripts.
Complete the inventory of additional explainers and presentation artifacts reported by the author.
Migrate the current Part II interface under /research/part-ii/ while preserving redirects.
